newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 12.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - By the year 2000, the housing market should become fully deregulated, according to the Minister for Local Development, Jaromir Schneider.

- Stanislav Devaty stepped down as the provisional director of the BIS, the Czech security agency. The BIS was recently accused of following Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux, although Devaty firmly denies the charge.

- Discussions on a collective agreement between the Railway Workers Union and the management of Czech Railways has not yet begun since such discussions should by law begin 60 days before the end of the year, according to the chairman of the union, Jaromir Dusak. Discussions should begin on November 15, although they will not concern wages.

- Deposits in small banks decreased by 14 percent in the third quarter of this year, while deposits in banks with forced administration decreased by 56 percent, according to the general manager of Banka Hana, Pavel Rucki. Deposits in branches of foreign banks increased by 50 percent.

- Kovosit Sezimovo Usti a.s. has signed a contract worth more than $20 million with America's Tree Machine Company for the delivery of shaping machines for customers in the United States, Mexico and South America.

- Brnenske Veletrhy a Vystavy a.s., the country's largest trade fair centre, posted a gross profit of 351 million crowns in the first nine months of 1996, an increase of 20 percent over the same period a year earlier. Sales reached 1.5 billion crowns in this period, an increase of 18 percent.
- Vodni Stavby a.s., the leading domestic construction firm oriented on industrial and energy projects, obtained a 50.1 percent controlling stake in Liberec's Interma a.s..
- A decision on the final form that the Czech refinery and petrochemical industry, in which the state-owned Unipetrol a.s. plays a decisive role, will take is likely be delayed by three months.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Industrial production increased by 8.4 percent in real terms in the first three quarters of 1996, and the results at the end of the year are expected to be similar. This is a slower increase than last year's 9.2 percent rise.
- Thanks to coupon privatisation, the Czech Republic leads the world in the number of shareholders compared with the total population.

- Even though less cigarettes have been sold so far this year compared with the same period last year, the actual number of cigarettes smoked has actually increased slightly. Since smokers were aware the price of cigarettes would increase in January this year due to an increase in tax, they bought more at the end of last year and less at the beginning of this year.

PRAVO - The trade surplus with CEFTA countries increased to 18.34 billion crowns in the first three quarters of 1996, an increase of more than 80 percent over the same period in 1995, according to the Czech Statistics Office.
